boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Galveston record (October 4, 1862) in Operations to Blockade the Texas Coast [September 1862-January 1863]. The four-day truce, the evacuation of the island to Virginia Point, the removal of guns and the later occupation are context; the compiler dates the action October 5. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: Renshaw demanded the surrender of the forts and then the unconditional surrender of the city. Cook, under standing orders to withdraw if the harbor could not be held, refused to surrender but asked time to remove women and children. Their accounts of the four-day truce differ: Cook says only that no new defenses were to be built or old ones strengthened and the fleet was not to approach; Renshaw says his understanding was that everything should remain as it was, and that the unwritten agreement let the Confederates carry off guns.
claims.rationale: Two interested accounts of an unwritten agreement; neither is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel Joseph J. Cook and Colonel X. B. Debray (Confederate) and Commander W. B. Renshaw (navy). Cook commanded at Galveston, answered the surrender demand and negotiated the truce; he says Debray reached the city on the night of the 4th and gave orders the next day. Renshaw commanded the flotilla and agreed the truce with officers of the other vessels present.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; Debray's part is described by Cook only. No automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Renshaw says his vessels captured the harbor defenses and city after a feeble resistance; Cook says the troops and material were removed and most of the population left before he withdrew to Virginia Point. NPS says the fall of Galveston closed a Confederate port.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Hebert's and Debray's reports (read, not selected), Wainwright's, Guest's and Law's reports, the removal of the guns in detail, returns and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cook's October 9, 1862 report and Renshaw's October 5 and 8, 1862 reports (ORN) are interested accounts from opposite sides. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
